Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) through VC/OAVM.
  In compliance with the provisions of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (“Act”), SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (“Listing 
Regulations”) and the MCA circulars, the AGM

9. Important Update on Transfer of Physical Shares
  Shareholders are requested to note that SEBI has 
prohibited the transfer of securities in physical form 
since 01st April 2019. However, to facilitate investors, 
SEBI has opened a special one-year window from 
05th February 2026 to 04th February 2027, allowing the 
re-lodgement of physical share transfer requests that 
were originally submitted before April 01, 2019, but 
returned due to documentation deficiencies.
  Shareholders wishing to avail themselves of this facility 
must submit their original share certificates, which is 
a mandatory requirement for processing the transfer 
under this special window. The complete details of the 
SEBI circular, can be accessed at https://greavescotton.

12.  Compulsory transfer of Equity Shares to Investor 
Education and Protection Fund (‘IEPF’) Account:
  In accordance with the provisions of sections 124 and 
125 of the Act and IEPF Authority (Accounting, Audit, 
Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 as amended from 
time to time (‘IEPF Rules’), dividends which remain 
unpaid or unclaimed for a period of seven years from 
the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account 
shall be transferred by the Company to the IEPF 
Account and such shares in respect of which dividend 
entitlements remained unclaimed for seven consecutive 
years or more are also required to be transferred by the 
Company to the IEPF Account.
  Members are requested to take note of the same and 
claim their unclaimed dividend immediately to avoid 
transfer of the underlying shares to the IEPF Account. 
The shares/dividend transferred to the IEPF Account 
can be claimed back by the concerned Members 
from IEPF Authority after complying with the procedure 
prescribed under the IEPF Rules.
  During the Financial Year 2025-26, all unpaid or 
unclaimed interim and final dividends for FY 2017-18 
were transferred to the IEPF. Following the conclusion of 
Financial Year 2025-26, the unclaimed interim dividend 
for FY 2018-19 was also transferred to the IEPF.
  During the Financial Year 2025-26, the Company 
transferred 77,834 Equity Shares to IEPF Authority. 
Consequently, as of 31st March 2026, IEPF Authority 
held a total of 18,40,555 Equity Shares of the Company. 
Following the conclusion of Financial Year 2025-26, 
the Company transferred an additional 42,230 Equity 
Shares to IEPF on 14th April 2026.
  Members who have not yet encashed or claimed their 
dividends from the FY 2020–21 final dividend onwards 
are requested to contact the Company or its RTA at 
the earliest to claim their outstanding dues. We have 
uploaded the details of such members on website of 
the Company, under the ‘Investors section’. Please note 
that no claim shall lie against the Company in respect of 
unclaimed dividend and shares transferred to the IEPF 
pursuant to the said Rules.

23. Dividend
 a.  In terms of the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 
2025, dividend paid or distributed by a Company 
on or after 1st April 2020 is taxable in the hands 
of its shareholders and therefore the Company is 
required to deduct income tax at source (“TDS”) 
on the dividend paid to its shareholders at the 
prescribed rates. The shareholders are requested 
to update/ register their PAN with the DP (if shares 
held in electronic form) and RTA/Company (if 
shares held in physical form).
 b.  No tax shall be deducted on the dividend 
payable to a resident individual shareholder 
during Tax Year 2026-27, if either of the below two 
conditions are fulfilled:
  i.  Total dividend paid/payable to a resident 
individual shareholder in the Tax Year 2026-27 
does not exceed ` 10,000/-.
  ii.  The resident individual shareholder has 
provided duly filled and signed Form 121 
with valid PAN, provided all the prescribed 
eligibility conditions are met.
   Resident shareholders whose dividend is liable for 
deduction of TDS at a concessional or Nil rate as 
per Section 395 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 can submit the necessary documents as mentioned in 
the Communication to shareholders on Taxation of 
Dividend Distribution available on the website of 
the Company at http://www.greavescotton.com/
investors/corporate-announcements to avail the 
benefit of lower rate of deduction or non-deduction 
of tax at source.
   As per Section 262 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, 
every person who has been allotted a PAN and 
who is eligible to obtain Aadhaar, shall be required 
to link the PAN with Aadhaar. In case of failure 
to link the Aadhaar with PAN, the PAN will be 
treated as in-operative and TDS will be deducted 
at a higher rate of 20% as per section 397 of the 
Income Tax Act, 2025.
 c.  Non-resident shareholders including Foreign 
Institutional Investors (FIIs) and Foreign Portfolio 
Investors (FPIs) can avail beneficial rates under tax 
treaty between India and their country of residence, 
subject to providing the following documents:
  i.  Self-attested copy of PAN card, if any, allotted 
by the Indian income tax authorities;
  ii.  Self-attested copy of Tax Residency 
Certificate (“TRC”) for the Tax Year 2026-27 
or calendar year 2026 obtained from the 
tax authorities of the country of which the 
shareholder is resident;
  iii.  Form 41 (erstwhile Form 10F) for the 
Tax Year 2026-27,
  iv.  Self-declaration for the Tax Year 2026-27 
by the non-resident shareholder of meeting 
treaty eligibility requirement and satisfying 
beneficial ownership requirement.

CHAIRMAN’S LETTER
We remain committed to harnessing 
our manufacturing and engineering 
excellence to grow our core business, 
at the same time drive growth through 
prudent organic and inorganic 
opportunities.”Dear Shareholders,
At Greaves Cotton Limited, we have consistently evolved with 
changing markets while maintaining a strong engineering 
foundation. For over 165 years, we have adapted to industrial, 
economic and technological shifts, while preserving the values 
that define our legacy. In the past two decades, we have 
become a diversified, multi-business, fuel-agnostic engineering 
enterprise with an expanding global perspective.
Today, Greaves Cotton operates through a synergistic ecosystem 
that includes Energy Solutions, Mobility Solutions, Industrial 
Solutions and purpose driven investee businesses. These areas 
position us to contribute meaningfully to India’s growth priorities 
in power reliability, last mile mobility, infrastructure development 
and financial inclusion.
As we enter the next phase, we are guided by Greaves.Next , 
our strategic roadmap to strengthen our position as a trusted, 
future-ready engineering company. This plan reflects our 
growth ambitions and our commitment to building a resilient 
organisation that creates lasting stakeholder value.
In Energy Solutions, we continued our shift from standalone 
equipment sales toward lifecycle based power solutions. 
Customer demand increasingly prioritises reliability and 
continuity, particularly across healthcare, industrial, data centres 
and infrastructure applications. By strengthening our services, 
spares and maintenance offerings alongside compliant, future 
ready products, we enhanced both customer engagement 
and the quality of revenue, positioning the business for 
sustainable growth.
Mobility Solutions remained a key growth driver. Our fuel 
agnostic powertrain portfolio reinforced our leadership in core 
segments and expanded into new applications and regions. 
The business gained momentum with the production of Euro V+ 
engines for microcars, now sold in several European countries. 
Our electric powertrain and aftermarket retail capabilities also 
advanced, demonstrating our commitment to clean 
mobility and long term relevance in evolving 
propulsion technologies.

Our strategy is anchored

across energy, mobility and

SUBSIDIARY COMPANIES
GREAVES ELECTRIC MOBILITY
Our investee businesses continue to shape Greaves’ future 
growth profile. The strategic investment made in the business of 
two and three-wheeler electric vehicles is once again gathering 
momentum. Electric two-wheelers business reported a 49% 
year-on-year growth, with its market share increasing from 3.5% 
in FY25 to 4.3% in FY26, reinforcing its position among the 
leading players in India’s electric two-wheeler market.
Greaves Electric Mobility has a customer base of over 4 lakh 
across its electric E2W and 3W portfolio in India. MLR Auto 
also sustained momentum, with consistent growth of 17% 
increase in VAHAN registrations in FY26 over the previous 
year. The momentum is expected to continue with a strong and 
growing order book. Equally significantly, the EBIT-level losses 
reduced substantially and are at ` 187.9 crore vis-à-vis ` 229.8 
crore in the previous year. We expect this trend to continue as 
volumes pick up and margins improve. A detailed report on 
GEML is included in the Annual Report further on.
GREAVES FINANCE
We are pleased to report that this subsidiary achieved a PAT 
positive result in FY26. The Company scaled up its digital-first, 
EV-focused lending platform, addressing a critical enabler of 
mass EV adoption. With the increased penetration of both E2W 
& E3W products in the Indian market, this platform is positioned 
for strong growth in the near future.
GREAVES TECHNOLOGIES
Greaves Technologies deepened its role as an engineering and 
R&D partner across automotive and industrial domains, moving 
steadily toward sustainable profitability.
CSR
Beyond business performance, we are deeply committed 
to responsible growth. We believe long-term value creation 
depends on sustainability, operational excellence, and 
inclusive development. Through our flagship program - SWATI, we continued to invest in empowering young women 
from underserved communities through employment-linked 
technical education and skill development. During the year, 
we extended the program to South India through an MOU with 
SASTRA in Tamil Nadu.
ESG
Our focus on safety, operational discipline and sustainability 
delivered strong ESG outcomes across parameters. 
Investments in energy efficiency, renewable power, waste 
reduction and people development demonstrate our 
commitment to inclusive and environmentally responsible 
growth. Our adherence to global best practices led to another 
year of zero incidents across our factories. Additionally, our new 
e-powertrain production line is operated entirely by a skilled and 
dedicated team of women.
Looking ahead, the external environment remains dynamic. 
We are confident in our ability to navigate change with a 
balanced portfolio, a strong balance sheet and disciplined 
execution. Our priorities are clear: scaling clean and reliable 
energy solutions, accelerating last mile mobility across 
fuel-agnostic platforms, strengthening services led revenue 
streams, and building technology and engineering capabilities 
for future industries.
Our journey is defined not only by growth, but also by relevance, 
resilience and responsibility. Every solution, capability, and 
partnership is aimed at building a future ready Greaves Cotton—
one that serves customers, empowers livelihoods and delivers 
lasting value for shareholders. And we aim to remain committed 
to contributing meaningfully to the nation’s development journey.
On behalf of the Board of Directors, I thank our shareholders for 
their continued trust and support. Your confidence strengthens 
our resolve to build a company that not only adapts to change 
but leads it with purpose.
Thank you for being part of this journey.
Yours sincerely,
Karan Thapar

MANAGING DIRECTOR & 
GROUP CEO’S LETTER
Dear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26, marked an important year for Greaves Cotton as 
we accelerated the execution of our Greaves.Next strategy 
across our core businesses. Rooted in our belief of Growth 
Powered by Legacy, we advanced with sharper strategic 
clarity and focus. Through this strategy, we aim to build on 
our strong engineering foundation to power the next phase 
of sustainable growth.
Within Greaves Cotton Limited, under Greaves.Next, 
our five-year growth roadmap is anchored around three 
strategic dimensions:
• Accelerating the Core by driving growth momentum 
across existing businesses 
• Building New Muscle onto the Core through new 
products, capabilities, and geographies 
• Expanding into New Horizons by leveraging our core 
strengths and engineering expertise 
Across these dimensions, we are committed to executing 
efficiently, scaling responsibly, and delivering sustainable 
results while building a stronger, more resilient organisation.
Greaves.Next in Action – From Intent to Impact
Over the past year, we moved decisively from intent to 
execution, by realigning the Greaves core organisation to 
support our strategy, enhance customer focus, and unlock 
synergies across core businesses and functions.

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Global Economy
The world economy demonstrated resilience throughout 
2025, effectively navigating evolving trade regulations and 
divergent regional performances. Substantial investments 
in technology mitigated the effects of emerging tariffs and 
shifting government policies, while global inflation moderated 
to a manageable 4.1%, with numerous countries achieving 
outcomes below initial market expectations.
The ongoing Russia-Ukraine war continues to disrupt global 
energy markets and supply chains, creating uncertainty for 
commodity prices and trade flows. Escalating Middle East 
conflicts further strain oil supplies and heighten inflationary 
pressures across economies. These developments 
challenge manufacturing sectors worldwide while testing 
international diplomatic responses.

16 Greaves Cotton Limited
Advanced economies achieved 1.9% 
growth, with the United States reaching 
2.1% through technology investments 
and policy backing. Emerging markets 
outperformed with 4.4% overall growth 
led by India’s strong 7.3% expansion 
and China’s steady 5.0% rise.

=== page 32 ===
Household consumption expanded steadily across global 
markets in 2025, propelled by heightened technology 
expenditures and wage growth in key economies. 
Consumers in the United States and emerging Asian nations 
increased spending on goods and services amid improving 
financial conditions, which helped cushion pressures from 
tariff implementations. Global job markets were resilient 
in 2025 despite trade disruptions and policy uncertainty. 
Technology and services sectors added jobs steadily 
while manufacturing growth slowed. Reliable employment 
levels supported rising household incomes and broader 
economic strength.
The services sector provided crucial support to global growth 
in 2025, expanding steadily even as trade in physical goods 
faced volatility. Finance technology services and tourism 
delivered solid performance, offsetting manufacturing 
weakness, particularly in Europe and Asia. This steady 
services expansion played a key role in keeping overall 
economic activity on track.
World GDP expanded by 3.4% in 2025, showing varied 
speeds across regions. Advanced economies achieved 
1.9% growth, with the United States reaching 2.1%  
through technology investments and policy backing.  
The euro area recorded 1.4% while Japan managed 
1.1%. Emerging markets outperformed with 4.4% overall 
growth led by India’s strong 7.3% expansion and China’s 
steady 5.0% rise.
World trade volumes accelerated to 4.1% growth in 2025, 
surpassing the previous year’s 3.6% expansion. A US-China 
trade truce substantially reduced tariffs and lifted restrictions 
on electronics components and critical minerals, alleviating 
prior tensions that had constrained global supply chains.The United States further eased select agricultural tariffs, 
restoring average rates to levels prevailing before recent 
escalations. These developments facilitated smoother 
cross-border commerce, particularly benefiting technology 
and commodity-dependent sectors across major economies.
Policy uncertainty moderated from late 2025 peaks 
yet remained elevated relative to 2024 baselines. 
Financial markets remained supportive despite occasional 
swings, with high-growth technology shares outperforming 
broader indices. Strong technology exports from Asia kept 
global trade flows steady.
Central banks managed inflation through calibrated 
adjustments, including interest rate reductions in the United 
States and the United Kingdom. These prudent measures 
preserved financial stability amid persistent trade frictions 
and evolving geopolitical developments.
(Source: World Economic Outlook (IMF))
Outlook
The global economy advances towards steady expansion 
projected at 3.6% for 2026, moderating slightly to 3.2% in 
2027. Technology-driven productivity gains, particularly 
from artificial intelligence integration across industry 
and healthcare sectors, propel this trajectory while 
counterbalancing persistent trade tensions and evolving 
political dynamics.
Advanced economies anticipate 1.8% growth in 2026. 
The United States leads with 2.4% expansion, bolstered by 
tax incentives under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and market 
recovery following the brief 2025 federal shutdown, creating 
favourable conditions for private investment and consumer

War Impacts
Closure of the US-Iran war disrupted a significant share of 
global oil and LNG supplies, pushing Brent crude prices 
above ~$120 per barrel and increasing natural gas costs, 
echoing the shocks of the 1970s. Oil production across Gulf 
states declined sharply, halting exports and triggering force 
majeure declarations by major energy producers.
Commodity volatility increased, with aluminium prices 
rising sharply after disruptions in Gulf production facilities, 
raising concerns for automotive, aerospace, electronics, 
construction, and food packaging costs. Further fertiliser 
disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz also heightened 
food-security risks. At the same time, inflation expectations 
remained elevated, with the euro area facing renewed price 
pressures and central banks maintaining a cautious stance, 
thereby increasing the risk of a more prolonged period of 
slower growth in energy-intensive economies.
World trade and growth suffered, with the IMF/World Bank 
downgrading 2026 GDP outlooks amid supply shortages, 
stock market declines, bond sell-offs, and currency instability; 
central banks delayed easing, exacerbating manufacturing 
challenges worldwide. Manufacturing sectors faced acute 
headwinds from energy costs and supply chain disruptions, 
testing diplomatic and economic resilience.
Indian Economy
The Indian economy exhibited robust performance  
throughout 2025-26, navigating global trade uncertainties 
and market volatility with commendable stability. 
Second Advance Estimates (SAE) project real GDP growth 
at 7.6% alongside Gross Value-Added expansion of 7.7%, 
underscoring the resilience of a domestic demand-led 
growth paradigm.India achieved a significant milestone by surpassing Japan 
to become the world’s fourth-largest economy, with a current 
GDP reaching $4.18 trillion. The nation remains on a trajectory 
to attain third-largest status by 2030, targeting $7.3 trillion, 
affirming its position as the fastest-growing major economy 
underpinned by resilient domestic demand and progressive 
structural reforms.
Strong agricultural output boosted rural incomes, providing 
essential stability to household spending patterns across 
the countryside. Concurrently, urban consumption gained 
momentum from consistent employment generation and 
moderated inflation pressures, reinforcing the structural 
strength of India’s consumption engine amid external  
headwinds.
Government spending on infrastructure like roads, railways, 
and defence will pick up again and keep going strong, helping 
industries grow. Private companies will also start investing 
more in manufacturing, real estate, and factory expansions. 
Manufacturing will keep growing steadily, though not as 
fast as before, showing reliable demand from businesses. 
Data centres and digital investments will become major new 
growth areas. Urban growth and new infrastructure projects 
will continue boosting construction and related industries. 
The power sector looks solid with nearly 475 GW capacity 
and almost no shortages (under 1%), so demand will shift to 
backup and standby power systems that ensure reliability.
Private consumption continues driving growth, supported 
by declining inflation and rising real incomes that enhance 
household purchasing power. Public capital expenditure 
of `12.2 lakh crore, as allocated in the Union Budget

War Impact
The 2026 US-Iran war has created significant challenges for 
the Indian economy, primarily through disruptions in global 
energy supplies. India imports around 85% of its crude oil 
requirements, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has led 
to sharp increases in Brent crude prices. 
Higher energy costs have pushed retail inflation projections 
for FY27, with the Reserve Bank of India facing difficulties 
in maintaining its target range. The rupee has depreciated 
due to increased demand for foreign exchange to cover 
elevated import costs. Food prices have also risen because 
of shortages in natural gas supplies that affect fertiliser 
production and agricultural inputs across the country.
Manufacturing industries such as automotive, chemicals 
and ceramics now face higher input costs from disrupted 
supplies of raw materials and other commodities. 
The outlook for the Indian 
economy remains positive 
and stable, with real GDP 
growth projected between 
6.8% and 7.2% for FY 2026-27. 
This trajectory underscores 
India’s capacity to sustain 
dynamic momentum amid 
prevailing global uncertainties.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW 
Energy Solutions Industry
In 2025, the Indian energy solutions landscape was shaped 
by a rapidly expanding power system infrastructure, 
accelerating renewable integration, and a growing ecosystem 
of storage, grid modernisation, and efficiency-oriented 
measures. Together, these developments supported a more 
reliable, affordable, and cleaner electricity supply.
The US-Iran war has put clear pressure on India’s energy 
sector by keeping global crude prices elevated and 
tightening supplies through the Gulf, forcing the country to 
pay more for the oil it imports while also adjusting domestic 
policies to cushion the blow. Higher benchmark prices, 
which have risen by around 50% since the conflict began 
and are holding above $100-120/barrel, have increased 
the cost of crude for Indian refiners and raised the risk of 
slower GDP growth and higher inflation, given India’s heavy 
dependence on imported oil. In response, the government 
has moved to soften the impact on consumers and critical 
industries by cutting excise duties on petrol and diesel, 
deploying emergency fuel stockpiles, and using targeted 
windfall taxes on certain fuel exports so that sufficient supply 
remains available for the domestic market, helping maintain 
some stability in fuel availability even as the external energy 
environment remains volatile.
India met a record peak power demand of 242.49 GW in  
FY 2025-26, underscoring the sector’s ability to balance 
rising consumption with adequate generation and 
transmission capacity. Per capita electricity consumption in India rose to 1,460 kWh 
in 2024-25, up 52.6% from 957 kWh in 2013-14, reflecting 
broader economic and demographic drivers. Rural power 
availability improved from 12.5 hours per day in 2014 to 
22.6 hours, while urban areas now enjoy up to 23.4 hours of 
supply, compared with 22.1 hours in 2014, highlighting the 
improvement in reliability and reach. RDSS-linked schemes 
have also enabled on-grid electrification of PVTG, tribal, 
and other priority-group households, with `6,521 crore 
sanctioned to energise about 13.65 lakh households and 
related public-use locations.
(Source: PIB)
Indian Genset Market
The Indian generator market serves as a critical backup 
and prime power solution across industrial, commercial, 
and residential segments, especially in regions where grid 
reliability does not fully match rising power demand intensity.
The Indian diesel generator market reached $1.66 
billion in FY25 and grew to $1.83 billion in FY26, with the  
market expected to expand at a CAGR of 7.18% over 
the next five years.This reflects sustained demand for 
reliable on site power generation, even as the national grid 
deficit narrows. This growth is underpinned by continued 
reliance on gensets in Tier II and Tier III cities, industrial 
segment, data centre and telecom, infrastructure, and 
construction-sector activity that runs ahead of formal 
grid-connection timelines.

yet displacing diesel as the primary solution for multi hour

Indian Automobile/Mobility Industry
The Indian automobile industry has reached a decisive 
stage in its development, with India now recognised 
as the world’s third-largest automobile market, having 
overtaken Japan in recent years. The sector’s valuation 
reflected rapid growth driven by strong domestic 
demand, government incentives, and a strategic shift 
toward electric vehicles (EVs). The Union Ministry 
for Road Transport and Highways, has reiterated the 
government’s ambitious goal of making India the world’s number one automobile manufacturing nation by 2030, 
supported by expanding exports, job creation, and 
large-scale infrastructure and sustainability initiatives.
This aspirational target rests on strong fundamentals, 
including rising income levels and urbanisation that sustain 
domestic demand, growing export volumes to global 
markets, and rapid technological transformation in design, 
connectivity, and electrification. The sector is also being 
reshaped by green mobility policies and production-linked 
incentive schemes, which are accelerating the adoption of 
EVs and hybrid technologies across passenger vehicles, 
two-wheelers, and commercial fleets. As a result, India is 
evolving from a cost competitive manufacturing base into a 
broader global mobility hub, with domestic manufacturers 
and global OEMs increasingly treating the country as a 
design, export, and innovation support centre.
Key Milestones:
• India is the world’s third-largest auto market
• Largest manufacturer of three-wheelers
• Second-largest manufacturer of two-wheelers
• Third-largest manufacturer of passenger vehicles  
globally
(Source: Ambedkar Chamber of Commerce and Industry)
The Indian automobile industry is steadily adapting to 
the electrification trend, with the 3-wheeler (L5) segment 
witnessing significant transformation. Over the past five 
years, electric vehicle adoption in this segment has grown 
from negligible levels to approximately 35% market share. 
This transition has largely been driven by a shift from CNG to 
electric powertrains, particularly in the 3-wheeler passenger 
vehicle segment. Consequently, the CNG segment has seen 
a notable decline, with its share reducing from approximately 
63% to around 35%.
The Union Ministry for Road Transport 
and Highways, has reiterated the 
government’s ambitious goal of making 
India the world’s number one automobile 
manufacturing nation by 2030, supported 
by expanding exports, job creation, 
and large-scale infrastructure and 
sustainability initiatives.

2-Wheeler & 3-Wheeler
The electric two-wheeler industry sustained steady 21% 
year-on-year growth, reaching nearly 1.4 million units in 
FY 2025-26 even after PM E-Drive subsidies tapered off. 
EV penetration accelerated rapidly to around 8% by the 
second quarter before experiencing a brief slowdown 
following GST 2.0 implementation, which cut GST rates on 
ICE two-wheelers from 28% to 18%, temporarily improving 
affordability of conventional petrol bikes compared to 
electric models.
Nevertheless, EV adoption rebounded strongly onto a growth 
path, propelled by electric vehicles’ compelling total cost 
of ownership advantages over ICE counterparts alongside 
enhanced product experiences delivered through fresh 
launches spanning multiple segments.
The L5 three-wheeler sector recorded a solid 17% year-on-
year volume growth in FY 2025-26, reaching nearly 8,00,000 
units for the for the financial year. Electric vehicle share 
jumped to ~33% for the full year from 23% in FY 2024-25, 
showing clear progress toward electrification.
Government support through PM E-Drive for L5 E3W 
continued until December 2025, when funding ran out ahead 
of schedule due to strong demand. Even without subsidies, 
L5 EV three-wheelers maintain consistent sales backed by 
new model launches and better financing terms. GST 2.0 
brought down rates on conventional three-wheelers from 
28% to 18%, making them more affordable, while electric 
adoption kept building momentum across the segment. 
Passenger three-wheelers emerged as the standout 
performer, with EV penetration jumping from 20.8% in 2024 
to 31.8% in 2025, peaking at nearly 39% of all passenger 
3Ws sold in December 2025.
The L3 E3W (e-rickshaw) sector posted 5% year-on-year 
growth in FY 2025-26. This highly fragmented and localised 
industry saw the top 10 OEMs’ market share drop further 
to under 30% of total volumes, while the number of players 
swelled with several new manufacturers entering the 
segment during the year. At the same time, the government signalled plans for stricter safety regulations aimed at raising 
product quality standards and enhancing customer safety. 
Additionally, the Govt. has extended the PM e-Drive subsidy 
benefit for L3 E3W (e-rickshaw segment) till 31st March 2028.
High-speed electric two-wheelers continue dominating 
volumes with 13,45,244 units sold, capturing the 
largest market share.

Engineering Research and Development (ER&D)
The Indian Engineering Research and Development (ER&D) 
Services market is a core pillar of the country’s digital 
product and manufacturing ecosystem, supplying software, 
embedded, and mechanical engineering intelligence that 
underpins automotive, semiconductor, industrial, telecom, 
and services led platforms. The sector is anchored to India’s 
large engineering base, cost efficiency, and its role as a 
global delivery hub for product geometry, electronics, and 
control software development.
The Indian ER&D Services market stood at $133.71 
billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to $147.27 billion 
in 2026 at a CAGR of 10.14%, reaching $238.63 billion 
by 2031. This growth is driven by the global shift toward 
digital engineering outsourcing, rising software content 
in products, and India-centric waves of domestic R&D in 
automotive, defence, and semiconductor-linked programs, 
which together deepen the longevity and value intensity of 
ER&D contracts.
By industry vertical, Automotive held the largest share 
with 28.10% of the India ER&D Services market in 2025, 
underpinned by large-scale ADAS calibration, e-powertrain, 
and connectivity platform development programmes for 
global and domestic platforms. However, Semiconductor 
and Electronics is the fastest-growing segment, projected 
to grow at 12.85% CAGR to 2031 and to add about $27 
billion in incremental value, driven by domestic chip design 
incentive schemes, PLI-linked Fab cluster policy, and 
multi-billion-dollar expansion announcements from players 
such as NXP. Industrial, transportation, construction, and 
heavy-machinery (ITCHM), services-led verticals such as 
BFSI and Healthcare, and Hi-tech-led verticals (software 
and internet, telecom, and IoT -providers) collectively round 
out the demand base, as cross sector adoption of AI, IoT, 
and cybersecurity mandated design increases the need for 
specialised ER&D support.

COMPANY OVERVIEW
Greaves Cotton Limited (referred to as ‘Greaves’ or ‘GCL‘ 
or ‘the Company’), is a trusted engineering company with 
a 165+ year legacy since 1859 and is headquartered in 
Mumbai, India. Over time, the Company has transformed 
from a pioneer in single-cylinder diesel engines into a 
diversified multi-business engineering platform with 
deep capabilities across engineering, aftermarket 
retail, finance, technologies, and electric mobility. 
Greaves delivers precision solutions for automotive, 
agriculture, marine, construction and railway sectors, 
manufacturing diesel, gasoline, petrol engines, pump 
sets, gensets, farm equipment and industrial engines.
Greaves continues to drive growth across its core 
and emerging business segments, supported by a 
steady focus on strengthening its operating base 
and expanding its market presence. Building on its 
core businesses, the Company’s strategic roadmap, 
Greaves.Next, is centred around Energy Solutions, 
Mobility Solutions, and Industrial Solutions. 
Greaves.Next reflects the Company’s commitment to 
strengthening core engineering capabilities, building 
new capabilities, expanding into adjacent markets, and 
scaling across geographies through sustained growth, 
organic & inorganic opportunities, and future-readiness. 
The Company’s investee businesses, including Greaves 
Electric Mobility Limited (GEML) and Greaves Finance 
Limited (GFL), extend its presence into consumer-facing 
segments. These businesses are being scaled to address emerging opportunities in electric mobility 
and financial services. Manufacturing facilities located 
in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Talegaon and other 
sites maintain world-class standards with Zero Liquid 
Discharge ISO certifications and advanced technologies 
like robotic spray painting, sensor-based systems and 
solar rooftops generating 5 million units annually.
Greaves serves diverse customer segments through 
reliable products, sustainable technologies, and 
customer-centric solutions. With its engineering 
legacy, diversified businesses, and growing portfolio 
of solutions, the Company is positioning itself as a 
future-ready engineering company that can support 
energy, mobility, and industrial applications with 
innovation and operational discipline.
GCL integrates sustainability across the Environment, 
Social, and Governance pillars, implementing 
energy-efficient BLDC fans, R32 AC systems, water 
recycling, green belts, and Zero Liquid Discharge at all 
plants. The Company has earned Great Place to Work 
certification for four years in a row. CSR flagship SWATI 
program empowers underprivileged young women

in the manufacturing sector at Symbiosis Indore and 
SASTRA Thanjavur campuses, enrolling 168 students 
since FY 2024-25. Safety awards from the National 
Safety Council highlight Zero Lost Time Injury and 
excellence in accident-free operations.

Overview
Greaves Energy Solutions pursues sustainable growth 
through a strategic evolution in its business model focussed 
on serving customers throughout the genset’s complete 
lifecycle, well beyond the initial equipment purchase. 
The company prioritises building enduring partnerships 
by expanding into high-margin recurring revenues through 
spares distribution, comprehensive service support and 
Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs). This lifetime value 
approach ensures continuous, reliable performance for 
customers while creating stable, predictable income streams 
that complement traditional genset sales and strengthen 
overall business resilience.
The Company now emphasises integrated power solutions 
rather than isolated genset products, combining hardware 
with energy management services, IoT monitoring and 
lithium-ion battery backups to deliver complete reliability 
packages. Demand patterns have evolved from addressing 
basic power deficits to prioritising uptime and operational 
continuity, especially for mission-critical applications like 
hospitals, malls and industrial facilities.
Aftermarket services and AMCs have become key 
differentiators, enabling Greaves to retain customers and 
capture higher margins through proactive maintenance, 
extended warranties and performance guarantees. 
Data centres represent a significant growth opportunity 
with potential demand exceeding `150 billion, driven by 
India’s digital infrastructure expansion and hyperscale 
computing needs.Outlook

technologically advanced electric drive systems.

cargo applications.

Risk & Concerns (Core Businesses)
Greaves Cotton Limited operates in a dynamic business environment and is exposed to various risks that may impact its 
operations, financial performance and growth trajectory. The key risks and concerns and corresponding mitigation measures 
are outlined below:
Technology Transition Risks
The industry continues to transition towards 
cleaner fuels, electric mobility and emerging 
technologies. Increasing adoption of alternate 
fuels, battery storage, hybrid and gas-based 
solutions, and software-led systems may impact 
demand for conventional products.The Company is expanding its portfolio across 
electric mobility, alternate fuels, hybrid and gas-based 
solutions, including the addition of electric powertrain 
systems as part of its offerings. The Company continues 
to strengthen its R&D and technology capabilities to 
remain aligned with evolving market trends.
Demand and Execution Risks
Demand remains linked to macroeconomic 
conditions, customer capex cycles and 
infrastructure activity. Delays in industrial or 
infrastructure capex, regulatory-led transitions or 
demand normalisation in certain segments may 
impact volumes.The Company continues to diversify across end-use 
segments, applications and geographies, while 
strengthening customer engagement. The Company 
is adopting a customer lifetime value approach 
and has reorganised its internal teams to enhance 
responsiveness and mitigate demand variability.
Competitive Intensity
The Company operates in competitive markets 
across its businesses. Pricing pressure, low-cost 
offerings, margin expectations in contracts, 
and the need to strengthen differentiated value 
propositions may impact profitability and 
market position.Focus on product quality, service capabilities, brand 
strength and differentiated offerings, along with 
continuous cost optimisation and value engineering, 
supports competitiveness and customer retention.Regulatory and Policy RisksRisk Mitigation
The Company’s businesses are subject to evolving 
regulatory requirements, including emission 
norms, fuel policies, EV incentive structures and 
product compliance standards. Any changes in 
government policies, particularly relating to diesel 
usage, alternate fuels or emission standards, may 
impact demand and cost structures.The Company continuously monitors regulatory 
developments and proactively aligns its product 
portfolio with evolving norms. The Company’s R&D 
teams actively work on emission norms roadmaps to 
ensure readiness for upcoming regulatory changes. 
Investments in fuel-agnostic technologies and compliant 
product platforms enable timely adaptation.

Greaves Electric Mobility Ltd 
Overview
Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML), the electric 
mobility arm of GCL, stands among India’s pioneers in the

fulfilling its mission to democratise smart, sustainable 
mobility solutions.

one of the industry’s widest ranges of electric scooters, 
holding several national and international records. GEML has 
established pockets of market leadership with ~12% market 
share in states which contribute to ~22% of overall industry 
volumes in E2W segment for H2 FY26. During the year, Ampere 
launched successful models, including Magnus Grand and 
Magnus G-Max, both warmly received by customers, while 
rolling out continuous technology and feature upgrades 
across the Nexus range with Nex.IO connectivity. GEML is also 
working on the next generation of products with the Magnus

is being positioned as an ‘ICE breaker’. The 6th Gen electric 
scooter is being designed with a vision to deliver better 
performance while offering better ownership economics with 
the potential to challenge high-selling petrol scooters in the 
sub-`  1 lakh price category.
GEML maintains a strong presence in the 3W segment 
through subsidiary entities MLR Auto Limited and Bestway 
Agencies Private Limited, addressing passenger and 
cargo needs in L5 3W (autos) and L3 3W (e-rickshaws)

GEML increased the equity stake in MLR Auto from 51% 
to a total of 67.41%, reinforcing control and alignment 
with long-term growth objectives. Additionally, GEML had 
secured regulatory approvals for its proposed Initial Public 
Offering (IPO) in May 2025. Recently, SEBI issued a circular 
granting a one-time, six-month relaxation for IPO observation 
letters expiring between April 1, 2026, and September 30,

are also influenced by geopolitical environment to decide

and margins, affirming a sustainable trajectory. The Company

trust in the Ampere brand’s quality and reliability.
GEML’s comprehensive portfolio spans slow-speed scooters

Greaves Finance Limited 
Overview
Greaves Finance Limited (GFL), operating under the brand 
ev.fin as a wholly-owned subsidiary of GCL, functions as 
an EV-focussed Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC). 
Initially launched in 2019 as a captive financier for Electric 
2-Wheelers (E2W), GFL has transformed into a brand-agnostic 
EV lending platform, powered by a fully digitised origination 
infrastructure that delivers loan approvals in under 2.5 minutes.
In FY 2025-26, ev.fin surpassed the landmark `500 crore 
Assets Under Management (AUM) (on owned and managed 
basis) milestone, reflecting disciplined growth, dynamic OEM 
partnerships, and geographic expansion to 74 cities across 
14 states, covering approximately 55% of the E2W market by 
volume, while maintaining strong portfolio performance.
GFL deepened its OEM ecosystem during the year, 
consistently ranking ev.fin among the top three financiers at 
key E2W dealerships. After building on collaborations with 
Ather (FY24) and River Mobility (FY25) & other top E2W 
OEMs, GFL formalised a preferred financier arrangement with 
Suzuki EV in FY 2025-26. This partnership delivers competitive 
financing options, including low-interest loans and residual 
value-backed products, to Suzuki’s expanding customer base.
The flagship Smart.fin product, featuring residual value (RV) 
guarantees through strategic OEM tie-ups, was relaunched 
with Ather in FY 2024-25 and extended to Suzuki EV in  
FY 2025-26. By addressing resale value uncertainty, a key 
barrier to EV adoption, Smart.fin enables customers to 
upgrade seamlessly to newer models, establishing ev.fin as 
a market differentiator.

In the financing domain critical to E2W mass adoption, the 
resale market for used E2Ws remains underdeveloped, 
complicating residual value assessments and collateral 
security despite nascent traction in pre-owned financing. 
Policy transitions, from FAME II to PM E-DRIVE, introduce

requiring enhanced asset tracking, digital lock-in mechanisms,

structural demand slowdown or technological disruption 
could disproportionately impair portfolio quality.

Resale market is at nascent stages, but GFL has piloted the 
end-to-end resale process on its repossessed assets including 
vehicle and battery valuation, refurbishment and reselling. 
GFL portfolio covers diverse mix of OEM and not concentrated 
on subsidy-depended OEMs. Additionally, subsidies over 
the years have reduced drastically but the demand has 
remained resilient.
Under B2C model, only assets with fixed battery architecture 
are onboarded, reduces the swap risk.  
Service-related issues are tracked early against location & 
OEM/dealership level to control the delinquency. Exposure is 
controlled with OEMs having thin after-sales services or resulting 
in higher delinquencies due to performance. 
Diversification planned to E3W segments & other assets to 
reduce E2W exposure overtime. Within E2W, portfolio is 
expanded across OEMs, geographies, retail (B2C)/gig (B2B) 
to control demand-related slowdown.
Strategic Outlook
The Company’s Greaves.Next strategy transforms the 
Company into a diversified solutions-led enterprise 
spanning Energy, Mobility, and Industrial Solutions, building 
upon its deep engineering and manufacturing heritage, 
while realigning the portfolio toward high-growth domains 
like energy transition, customer life-time value, and 
technology-driven services.
The next phase emphasises execution-driven expansion, 
strengthening core B2B operations and operational efficiencies alongside sustained investments in building 
capabilities in serving new products, new customers, 
and new markets. Enhanced integration across business 
verticals will enable comprehensive ecosystem offerings that 
seamlessly combine energy solutions and mobility platforms, 
creating superior value for customers.
Strategic priorities track structural market shifts. 
Energy Solutions will prioritise clean distributed 
power systems, addressing rising reliability needs. 
Mobility operations target scaled presence in electric last-mile 
applications complemented by export opportunities, robust 
powertrain development, and aftermarket service expansion. 
Company-wide efforts focus on boosting service revenue 
contributions, penetrating export markets and advancing 
product innovation through technology investments.
Capital deployment follows a measured approach, 
channelling resources into core business sustainability, 
high-return growth verticals and selective strategic 
initiatives. This framework balances expansion ambitions 
with financial discipline, ensuring capital efficiency while 
maintaining healthy balance sheet metrics and shareholder 
value creation.
India’s accelerating EV adoption, decentralised energy 
demand, and global appetite for competitive engineering 
solutions create powerful tailwinds for Greaves’ diversified 
portfolio. These dynamics align directly with the Company’s 
strategic positioning across stable cash-generative 
operations and scalable growth platforms.
Greaves maintains rigorous portfolio evaluation centred 
on capital productivity and business performance as a 
cornerstone of Greaves.Next execution. This disciplined 
approach, combined with improving operational execution 
and clear strategic direction, positions Greaves to deliver 
sustained growth, profitability and long-term stakeholder 
value through its transformed business model. 
The electric mobility business has built a strong foundation 
with a diversified and robust product portfolio, strong 
dealer footprint and aftersales support. Greaves Electric 
Mobility is poised to strengthen its market position through 
a multi-pronged strategy focussed on product, network, 
and channel expansion. The planned launch of the Magnus 
6th Gen, positioned as a strong “ICE breaker” in the mass 
segment, underpins its push toward product diversification 
and wider consumer adoption. At the same time, the company 
is accelerating network penetration into under-served and 
weaker markets to unlock incremental demand, while also 
building alternate sales channels – including e-commerce 
platforms – to enhance accessibility and improve customer 
reach beyond traditional dealerships.

Program Collaborations and Progress
Greaves Cotton Limited launched the SWATI Program in 
collaboration with Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences 
(SUAS) in Indore. The partnership offers two residential 
diploma courses for underprivileged girls. Diploma in 
Manufacturing Automation (DMA) serves 12th pass students 
(Science with Mathematics) over two years. Diploma in 
Advanced Manufacturing Excellence (DAME) targets 10th 
pass students over three years.
In FY 2024-25, the first batches started in August 2024 at 
the SUAS Indore campus. These included 74 students (18 
in DMA and 56 in DAME). All students completed their first 
year without any dropouts. In FY 2025-26, second batches 
began in August 2025, enrolling 64 students total (33 in DMA 
and 31 in DAME).
The Company expanded the SWATI Program to South India 
in FY 2025-26 through an MoU with Shanmugha Arts Science 
Technology and Research Academy (SASTRA) in Thanjavur, 
Tamil Nadu. This partnership offers a two-year Diploma in 
Manufacturing for 12th pass (Science with Mathematics) 
students. The first batch started in March 2026, enrolling  
30 students at the SASTRA Thanjavur campus.
Skill Development Goals
The SWATI Program builds technical skills and employability 
through industry-relevant education and hands-on training. 
Young women gain exposure to advanced manufacturing 
technologies in a residential learning environment. 
By providing access to quality education, Greaves promotes 
financial independence and self-reliance among women 
from marginalised communities. This effort supports 
the Company’s commitment to social responsibility and 
inclusive growth.

INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS AND THEIR 
ADEQUACY
The Company has robust internal control systems in place, 
commensurate with the size, complexity and industry 
in which it operates. The Company’s adherence to the 
Committee of Sponsoring Organisations of the Treadway 
Commission (“COSO”) framework and assessment of internal 
financial controls in line with Indian regulatory guidelines 
further underscores its dedication to transparency and 
accountability. The Company ensures that the systems are 
periodically upgraded to keep pace with changing norms 
and ensure their effectiveness. 
The Company has adopted policies and procedures that 
guide day-to-day activities across all major functions. 
These controls are designed to give reasonable assurance on: 
• Accuracy and completeness of the financial records. 
• Compliance with applicable laws and regulations. 
• Effectiveness and efficiency of business operations. 
• Prevention and detection of fraud and errors. 
• Safeguarding of Company assets from unauthorised 
use or losses. 
The company’s Corporate Governance Policies and Code 
of Conduct provide a strong foundation for transparency, 
accountability, and ethical decision-making. By clearly 
defining roles, responsibilities, and authorities, these 
policies ensure effective governance and oversight. 
Wide communication of these policies across the 
organisation promotes a culture of compliance and integrity. 
This framework supports informed decision-making, 
protects stakeholders’ interests, and upholds the 
company’s reputation. 
Employees are benefited by a well-defined whistleblower 
policy that ensures and encourages reporting of any 
misconduct, unethical behaviour or any behaviour with the 
possibility of conflict of interest. Highest standards of integrity and transparency are adhered to and further encouraged by 
a self-monitoring mechanism. 
Regular reviews by management and the Audit Committee, 
along with internal audits, help maintain a robust control 
environment. During FY 2025-26, key controls were 
adequately tested, and appropriate remedial measures 
were initiated, where deviation from standard practices was 
identified. The internal audit team regularly follows up on 
the implementation of corrective actions and improvements 
in business processes. The Company is also committed 
to ensuring that the operations are carried out within the 
purview of applicable laws and statutory requirements. 
Internal Audit 
The Company has an in-house internal audit team consisting 
of qualified professionals. This team prepares an annual 
audit plan based on risk assessment and regularly reviews 
financial, operational and compliance controls. The Company 
also engages reputed third-party firms to support and 
complement the in-house team’s work. Audit findings are 
shared with the management, and corrective actions are 
taken as needed. The Audit Committee of the Board closely 
monitors the internal audit activities. It meets at least four 
times a year to review audit plans, key findings and the 
status of follow-up actions. The Internal Audit function 
plays an important role in giving the management and 
the Audit Committee an independent view of the internal 
control systems and effectiveness of the risk management 
processes and the status of compliance with operating 
systems, internal policies and regulatory requirements 
across the company and its subsidiaries. 
During the year, internal controls were reviewed and 
tested, and no significant weaknesses were found in their 
design or operation.

NATURE OF BUSINESS
Greaves Cotton Limited is a diversified, future-ready, and 
trusted engineering company with a rich legacy of over 165 
years, impacting millions of lives every day. Under its strategic 
framework GREAVES. NEXT , the Company has sharpened its 
focus across key business areas - Energy Solutions, Mobility 
Solutions, Industrial Solutions (IS), NBFC, and Technologies. 
Through these, Greaves delivers a comprehensive portfolio 
of engineering products and solutions, including gensets, 
engines, aftermarket services, e-powertrain systems, 
electric mobility solutions, and ER&D technologies, catering 
to diverse applications across sectors.
The Company operates five state-of-the-art manufacturing 
facilities across India on standalone basis and is supported by 
a widespread distribution and service network spanning the 
country. This robust ecosystem enables strong aftermarket 
and retail reach while ensuring consistent customer support 
and service excellence. With a continued commitment 
in nation-building, Greaves actively contributes to the 
Government of India’s ‘Make in India’ initiative by developing 
and manufacturing world-class products domestically.
During the year under review, there has been no change in 
the nature of the business of the Company.

ENVIRONMENT, HEALTH AND SAFETY
The Company’s manufacturing units are governed by 
‘Environment Policy’ and ‘Health and Safety Policy’ and 
are certified as per ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 assessment 
standards. The Company has various safety guidelines in 
place which help to identify unsafe actions or conditions at 
the Company premises. These guidelines form the corner 
stone on which the Company can operate smoothly, devoid 
of any mishap or accidents at the workplace. The Company 
takes various steps to promote environment, health and safety 
measures across the Company, which, inter alia, include:
Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Initiatives
A. Workplace Safety Initiatives
 Infrastructure & Equipment Safety
 1.  Installed road-safety solar studs along internal 
company roadways to improve visibility and 
minimize accident risk.
 2.  Deployed beam detector lights on forklifts to 
enhance operational safety during material 
handling activities.
 3.  Introduced a biometric authentication system for 
forklift operators to restrict equipment access 
strictly to authorized personnel.
 4.  Installed spark arresters in the testing area to 
mitigate potential fire hazards. Fire Safety & Emergency Preparedness
 1.  Upgraded the fire-hydrant network with SS-coupling, 
triple-layered canvas hoses to strengthen fire-safety  
infrastructure.
 2.  Installed a digital water-level indicators for 
the fire-hydrant system to enable continuous 
monitoring and timely response readiness.
 3.  Deployed portable eyewash units across the shop 
floor to enhance emergency preparedness.
 Systems, Governance & Risk Management
 1.  Implemented an online work-permit system 
to streamline tracking and ensure timely 
approval of permits.
 2.  Rolled out a barcode based tracking system 
for reporting unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, 
and near-miss incidents to strengthen 
safety governance.
 3.  Conducted periodic Safety Management Audits to 
identify latent hazards and accident-prone areas.
 4.  Maintained a robust safety regime through 
continuous Safety Management Assurance 
Technique audits, internal audits, theme-based 
inspections, safety patrolling, and routine fire/
emergency equipment checks.
 Safety Culture, Training & Engagement
 1.  Executed a comprehensive monthly safety 
training calendar covering safety, health & 
environment for all the plant employees, with 
training effectiveness measured through pre-and 
post-assessment sessions.
 2.  Visitor safety guideline card distributed at 
entry gates to ensure visitor compliance with 
on-site safety norms.
 3.  Conducted regular safety drives and 
audits to elevate employee awareness and 
operational readiness.
 4.  Fostered a safety-positive workplace culture 
by integrating process and behavioral 
safety methodologies to drive toward a 
zero-accident target.
 5.  Enhanced workforce engagement through safety 
oath ceremonies and interactive competitions 
(including poster, slogan, poem, and essay 
contests) during National Safety Week.

RecognitionB.  Occupational Health & Well-being
 1.  Provided complimentary health check-up &

 2.  Conducted annual medical health check-up

 3.  Organised various health programs like blood 
donation camps, neuropathy, eye check-up, 
tetanus toxoid vaccination camp and sessions on 
stress management, brain stroke, etc.
C.  Infrastructure & Facility Improvements
 1.  Implemented sensor based lighting systems 
across common areas like corridors, enabling 
automated illumination control. This ensures that 
lights switch on only when activity is detected, 
thereby reducing energy consumption and 
preventing unnecessary usage.
 2.  Implemented robotic spray painting for 
industrial engines, achieving approximately 20% 
reduction in paint consumption while reducing 
operator exposure to hazardous conditions and 
lowering VOC emissions.
 3.  Implemented energy efficient BLDC fans in Unit-1 
at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to reduce overall 
power consumption.
 4.  Installed RECD kits across all gensets in every plant 
to optimise fuel usage and minimise emissions.
 5.  Replaced older air-conditioning units using R22 
refrigerant with environmentally friendly R32-based 
systems to enhance energy efficiency and lower 
environmental impact.
Environmental Sustainability Initiatives
A. Emission and Energy Management
 1.  Switched to Express feeder power supply to 
significantly reduce grid power failure occurrences, 
resulting in lower generator operating hours.
 2.  Commissioned a 700 KW solar power plant 
at the Industrial Engines Unit, Chikalthana, 
Sambhajinagar, which is expected to generate 
approx. 10,02,400 units of electricity annually.
 3.  Undertook efforts to reduce carbon footprint by 
recycling and reusing aluminium scrap briquettes 
in collaboration with suppliers.B. Water Conservation and Management
 1.  ETP/ STP water which is treated and recycled 
was previously used only for gardening purposes, 
which is now used for various processes like 
washroom flushes, floor cleaning etc. so that the 
water again goes to ETP/STP and can be later 
reused again. This ensures optimum usage of the 
water at plant.
 2.  Upgraded water distribution system from manual 
to automatic with electromagnetic flow meters 
which not only monitors the consumption but also 
ensures no water is wasted. Additionally process 
wise water lines have been installed reducing the 
losses and ensuring optimal usage of water.
 3.  Constructed artificial farm lakes at the Chhatrapati 
Sambhajinagar plant for water conservation 
and replenishment.
C. Digital & Green Operations
 1.  Deployed digital SOPs, check-sheets and 
reporting tools on the shop floor, promoting 
paperless operations.
 2.  Digital Environmental Monitoring Boards at 
all plants showing real-time environmental 
parameter data.
D. Waste Reduction & Eco-Friendly Packaging
 1.  Promoted the use of recyclable pallets for 
transporting finished goods.
 2.  Adopted moulded pulp packaging for finished 
components, which is both biodegradable 
and recyclable.
E. Afforestation & Green Belt Development
 1.  Celebrated World Environment Day and Earth 
Day through employee engagement and 
plantation drives.
 2.  Undertook afforestation using the Miyawaki 
plantation method, planting around 1,200 saplings 
at and around the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant.
 3.  Continued development of green belts around 
factory premises.
 4.  Developed a kitchen garden within the 
plant premises.

Disclosures pertaining to the Sexual Harassment of 
Women at the Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition 
and Redressal) Act, 2013
The Company is committed to provide a safe, respectful, 
and inclusive workplace for all its employees. In accordance 
with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women 
at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 
2013 (‘POSH Act’) and the Rules framed thereunder, the 
Company has adopted a Policy on Prevention, Prohibition 
and Redressal of Sexual Harassment at the Workplace 
(‘POSH Policy’). The weblink of the POSH Policy is provided 
in the Corporate Governance Report which forms a part of 
this Annual Report.
The Company has constituted an Internal Complaints 
Committee (‘ICC’) for receiving and redressing complaints of 
sexual harassment at the workplace. The composition of the 
ICC is in line with the requirement stated under POSH Act. 
During the year under review, the Company did not receive 
any complaints pertaining to sexual harassment.
The Company conducts periodic awareness sessions and 
training programmes for employees to foster understanding 
of the POSH Act and promote a culture of dignity and respect 
at the workplace.

POLICY ON APPOINTMENT AND REMUNERATION 
OF DIRECTORS
The NRC is entrusted with the responsibility of identifying 
and recommending candidates for appointment and 
re-appointment as Directors on the Board. As part of its role, 
the NRC undertakes an evaluation including a gap analysis 
of the Board’s existing structure where required, to ensure 
that the Board collectively possesses the requisite skills, 
expertise, and diversity with the Company’s requirements. 
Appointments recommended by the Committee are placed 
before the Board for consideration and, wherever appropriate, 
are thereafter recommended to the Shareholders for 
their approval.
Pursuant to the recommendations of the NRC and approval 
of the Board, the Company has adopted a Policy on 
appointment and remuneration of Directors, Key Managerial 
Personnel and Senior Management, which sets out the 
criteria for determining qualifications, positive attributes and 
independence of Directors. The criteria, inter alia, requires 
that a person proposed to be appointed to the Board 
possesses integrity, relevant qualifications, skills, experience 
and knowledge across areas such as engineering, banking, 
management, finance, marketing, legal, ESG and a proven 
track record. The Policy is available on the Company’s 
website, the weblink of which is provided in the Corporate 
Governance Report forming part of this Annual Report.
The Company recognises the importance of Board diversity 
as a key element in enhancing effective decision-making 
and sustaining long-term value creation. A diverse Board, 
comprising individuals with varied skills, experience, 
knowledge, perspectives, background, gender and other 
attributes, strengthens governance and overall corporate 
performance. Accordingly, the Board has adopted a Policy on Board Diversity, which sets out the framework 
for promoting diversity in the composition of the Board of 
Directors. The Policy is available on the Company’s website, 
the weblink of which is provided in the Corporate Governance 
Report forming part of this Annual Report.
The NRC periodically reviews and oversees succession 
planning for the Board and Senior Management as part of 
the Company’s talent management framework, ensuring 
continuity in leadership and alignment with the Company’s 
long-term objectives.
The details relating to the composition of the Board and its 
Committees, tenure of Directors, areas of expertise, criteria 
for payment of remuneration to Non-Executive Directors, 
and other relevant disclosures are set out in the Corporate 
Governance Report, which forms part of this Annual Report.
During the year under review, the Managing Director & Group 
CEO of the Company did not receive any remuneration or 
commission from any subsidiary of the Company.

RISK MANAGEMENT
The Company has constituted a Risk Management 
Committee of Directors to assist the Board in discharging its 
oversight responsibilities with respect to the Company’s risk 
management framework and practices.
The Company has implemented a robust Enterprise Risk 
Management (‘ERM’) Policy that encompasses strategic, 
operational, regulatory, geopolitical and catastrophic risks and provides for the clear identification of Risks That 
Matter (‘RTMs’). These RTMs are periodically assessed and 
monitored by the Management and are regularly reviewed 
by the Risk Management Committee.
The effective implementation of the ERM Policy enables 
the Board and the Management to ensure that risks 
which may have a significant impact on the Company are 
appropriately identified, monitored, and mitigated through 
timely and well-defined actions aimed at minimizing their 
potential impact.
Based on the assessment and in the opinion of the Board, 
there are no material risks that threaten the existence of the 
Company. However, certain risks that may warrant attention 
are detailed in the Management Discussion and Analysis 
section, forming part of this Annual Report.

VIGIL MECHANISM
The Company has established a robust vigil mechanism 
through its Whistle Blower Policy, which enables Directors, 
Employees, and Other Persons to report genuine concerns 
or grievances relating to unethical or unacceptable 
business practices. This vigil mechanism serves as an 
important corporate governance tool that not only facilitates 
the detection of fraud but also aids in the prevention and 
deterrence of misconduct.
To create awareness about the vigil mechanism, the Company 
regularly conducts Code of Conduct training programmes 
across its various locations. The mechanism provides direct 
access to the Compliance Officer or where necessary 
to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee for Directors, 
Employees, and Other Persons to report their concerns.
The Company is committed to ensuring that genuine Whistle 
Blowers are accorded complete protection from any form of 
unfair treatment or victimisation.
The Policy is available on the Company’s website and can 
be accessed at the weblink provided in the Corporate 
Governance Report forming part of this Annual Report.INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS RELATED TO

 Operational and Process Efficiencies
•  Aluminium Scrap Recycling: Partnered with supply

energy consumption and greenhouse gases 
emissions typically associated with aluminium 
heating and extraction.
•  Product & Process re-engineering: Undertook 
re-engineering initiatives at the shop floor level, 
resulting in reduced consumption of consumables, 
energy savings and minimised process waste.
•  Digitisation of operations: Transitioned shop floor 
operations to digital platforms by implementing 
digital SOP’s, check-sheets and reports, promoting 
paperless work culture.
 Renewable Energy
•  Solar Power Generation: Generated approximately 
5 million units of electricity through the solar power 
plants installed at the plants.
 Infrastructure & Facility Upgrades
•  Implemented sensorbased lighting systems 
across common areas like corridors, enabling 
automated illumination control. This ensures that 
lights switch on only when activity is detected, 
thereby reducing energy consumption and 
preventing unnecessary usage.
•  Switched to Express feeder power supply to 
significantly reduce grid power failure occurrences, 
resulting in lower generator operating hours.
•  Implemented energy-efficient BLDC fans in Unit-1 
at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to reduce overall 
power consumption.
•  Installed RECD kits across all gensets in every plant 
to optimise fuel usage and minimise emissions.
•  Replaced older air -conditioning units using R22 
refrigerant with environmentally friendly R32-based Annexure 2

systems to enhance energy efficiency and lower 
environmental impact.

and improvements in water pump efficiency.

JH check sheet for individual machines has also 
been digitalised and data from the digital check sheet 
is recorded and analysed to take up theme-based 
projects to improve equipment efficiency.
The station wise Standard operating procedures 
(SOPs) at our Chikalthana plant have also been 
digitised completely.
Automatic Guided Vehicles (AGVs): AGVs are 
material-handling machines that are autonomous and 
driverless. We have deployed AGV at locations having 
repetitive material movement. This has improved the 
productivity and eliminated the manual fatigue involved 
in manual material movement.
Online SPC monitoring system: Statistical Process 
Control (SPC) is a methodology used to monitor, control, 
and improve processes. Real-Time SPC Software takes 
this a step further by providing immediate data insights 
and analysis, enabling us to make informed decisions 
as events unfold on the shop floor
Digital Gemba Display / Digital Production 
Tracker:  This dashboard gives the real time status 
of the production in the plant by displaying live 
status of engines assembled, engines tested and 
engines dispatched.
Online check sheet for fixture PM: We have 
implemented a digital check sheet for the fixture 
maintenance activities conducted on the shop floor. 
This not only reduces the usage of paper-based check 
sheets but also improves the quality and consistency 
of maintenance work. Moreover, the data and insights from digital checklists can be leveraged to optimize 
maintenance strategies and improve decision making.
Robotic AI Vision Based Inspection system: Robotic 
AI Vision Based Inspection system for Pre-dispatch 
inspection of single cylinder engines. Deployed a 
robotic vision-based AI Inspection at the pre-dispatch 
inspection station that minimizes human intervention and 
creates an effective quality gate to identify NG engines, 
providing data traceability and 100% accuracy.
Digital Contract Labour Management System:  Digital 
Contract Labour Management System implemented 
across all the plants. The Contract Labour Management 
System delivers significant operational and financial 
benefits by ensuring 100% accurate attendance 
tracking through a Face ID–based system, eliminating 
manual errors and enabling precise report generation. 
It strengthens manpower planning and workforce 
management, which provides paperless and automated 
statutory compliance, and supports error free reporting 
for all contract workers.
Digital end-of-line (EOL) inspection: Digital end-of-
line (EOL) inspection with laser marking ensures that 
every component meets strict quality standards before 
dispatch. The system uses multigauging equipment to 
automatically measure and verify all critical dimensions, 
eliminating the possibility of human error. Only when 
all parameters meet specifications does the part 
proceed to laser barcode marking, which permanently 
encodes traceable data onto the component. 
This fully digital, mistakeproof process enables zero 
defect manufacturing, complete data traceability, 
and significantly enhances customer confidence 
by ensuring high dimensional accuracy and robust 
compliance documentation.
Digital Safety Work Permit System:  The Digital 
Safety Work Permit System is an automated platform 
that streamlines the creation, approval, and monitoring 
of work permits, ensuring safer and more efficient 
execution of onsite activities. It eliminates manual errors 
through real time validations, provides clear traceability 
of approvals, and enhances compliance with safety 
standards. The system enables digital checklists, 
geo-tagged monitoring, and instant alerts, thereby 
strengthening operational control and reducing risk 
across the workplace.
Barcode Based Safety Reporting System: 
Implemented a barcode based system to digitally 
capture and track unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, 
and nearmiss incidents. The system enables instant 
reporting from the shop floor, ensuring accurate location

export oriented operations.

1.  COMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE 
GOVERNANCE
Corporate Governance is deeply embedded in the 
Company’s culture and serves as the cornerstone of 
its approach to ethical, transparent, and responsible 
business conduct. The Company’s philosophy on 
corporate governance is founded on principles of 
fairness, accountability, integrity, and transparency, 
which guide all aspects of its operations and 
decision-making processes.
The Company firmly believes that strong corporate 
governance is essential for building sustainable 
businesses and long-term stakeholder trust. 
Its governance framework is designed to balance the 
interests of all Stakeholders - shareholders, employees, 
customers, communities, and society at large, while 
ensuring that business activities are conducted in 
compliance with applicable laws and regulations, in both letter and spirit, and in alignment with the 
highest standards of ethical conduct. These practices 
enable effective management, prudent risk oversight, 
and responsible value creation for the benefit of the 
Stakeholders, including in the execution of its strategic 
initiatives such as GREAVES.NEXT, a future-ready 
business strategy for sustainable growth in Energy, 
Mobility, and Industrial Solutions.
The Company is committed to the continuous adoption 
and strengthening of best-in-class governance 
practices, benchmarked against evolving regulatory 
requirements and global best practices. Sustainability, 
accountability, and responsible corporate citizenship 
remain integral to the Company’s governance 
philosophy and its pursuit of long-term value creation.
The Company is guided by its core philosophy of 
“Pancha Tatva – 5 Values, 1 Way of Life”.

2. BOARD OF DIRECTORS (‘BOARD’)
The Board is responsible for:
• Directing company operations efficiently to satisfy 
both stakeholder ambitions and broader ESG 
responsibilities.
• Guiding and approving major corporate strategies, 
risk policies, annual budgets, capital expenditures, 
and business plans.
• Safeguarding impartial decision-making by 
strategically assigning non-executive board 
members to areas prone to conflicts of interest.
• Balancing strategic mentorship for management 
with rigorous independent performance oversight.
• Periodically auditing and updating 
internal governance practices to sustain 
long-term effectiveness.The Company maintains a clear distinction between the 
role of the Board and that of Management, wherein the 
Management is responsible for execution of strategy 
and day-to-day operations, in alignment with the 
framework and policies approved by the Board.

The Chairman of the Company is a Non-Executive Director and is not related to the Managing Director & Group CEO. 
There are no inter-se relationships among the Directors.
The Chairman leads the Board, driving its integrity and cultivating a collaborative culture dedicated to the long-term benefit 
of the Company and its stakeholders. In addition to presiding over all Board and shareholder meetings, the Chairman 
facilitates seamless communication among directors and oversees board organization, composition, and effectiveness.
Working closely with the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Chairman plays a pivotal role in Board succession 
planning, director induction, and committee alignment. Furthermore, he actively guides the annual board evaluation 
process, meeting individually with directors to provide constructive feedback and strategic advice.
 Independent Directors
Independent Directors serve as the cornerstone of our corporate governance framework, bringing unbiased perspective 
and diverse expertise to the boardroom.
The Company has received formal confirmations from all Independent Directors, establishing compliance across 
three core areas:
• Independence Criteria: All Independent Directors meet the statutory eligibility requirements outlined under 
Regulation 16(1)(b) and 25(8) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, alongside Section 149 of the Act.
• Objective Judgment: Each director has affirmed that they are free from any current or foreseeable circumstances 
that could compromise their independent judgment or subject them to external influence.
• Databank Registration: All existing Independent Directors have confirmed their registration with the Independent 
Directors Databank maintained by the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), pursuant to Rule 6 of the Companies 
(Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014.
Based on the disclosures received from all the Independent Directors and in the opinion of the Board the Independent 
Directors fulfill the conditions of Independence as specified in the Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations, and are 
independent of the Management.
 Familiarisation Programmes
Pursuant to the requirements of Schedule IV of the Act and Regulation 25(7) of SEBI Listing Regulations, the Company 
has established a structured familiarisation framework divided into initial induction and continuous learning:
Onboarding & Induction: Newly appointed directors undergo a comprehensive orientation program featuring 
presentations by the management to introduce them to the Company’s operations, culture, and governance practices.
Ongoing Familiarisation: To ensure continuous learning, regular updates are integrated into Board and Committee 
meetings. These sessions cover long-term business strategies, brand architecture, budgets, subsidiary operations, and 
regulatory updates, alongside PESTLE-framed risk assessments and CSR initiatives. These meetings, complemented 
by periodic factory visits, provide directors with direct opportunities to interact with senior management and gain on-the-
ground operational insights.
